headline: A machine-learning study of 902 recordings suggests that the group rumbles of wild African elephants carry coordinated messages, not just overlapping noise.
score_reason: Modest, early result published on 1 Oct; one point below the pool score.
importance_line: Researchers who study animal communication get a method for reading whole choruses, but the model is only better than chance and the authors say more research is needed.
summary: Smithsonian Magazine reports on a study published on 1 Oct 2026 in Scientific Reports in which researchers trained a machine-learning model on 902 rumble recordings from elephants in Kenya's Amboseli National Park and found it predicted what the elephants were doing better than chance, though with many mistakes. The authors say choruses may carry extra fine-grained information, with rumbles becoming more alike during greetings, contact calls and slow group activity, but more research is needed to test what that means.
